chunks: And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The testimony of the Muslim slave is valid against the free Muslim.

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: the free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim; here indicating the witness’s religious identity
key_terms.تَجُوزُ: is valid or permissible in legal effect
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: testimony given in a legal or judicial setting

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Muslim slave accepted against a free Muslim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning admissible testimony, affirming that the testimony of a Muslim slave is accepted against a free Muslim. It reflects a juridical principle that Islam and probative integrity may establish testimonial validity in this case.
